knowledge_misuse: KR-GD-012 (applicability 'Power-module gate drives') tagged 'direct' for a discrete TO-247-4 design; it is applied by analogy and should be 'adapted' (conclusion unaffected).

KR-IS-001: the rule's recorded conflict (TI TIDA-010054 Eq. 30 with factor 2, EC-014) was not preserved; the controller/aux agent used the factor-2 form, so the two results size the same modules differently (0.119 W vs 0.2375 W gate power per channel).

KR-GD-003: the exclusion ('clamp not strictly needed with low R_G and low-inductance routing') was effectively invoked through an 'inherently immune' conclusion that rests on a non-conservative capacitance-divider bound (small-signal ratio at 1000 V); the clamp must be classed as required until the PRD-06933 off-state V_GS measurement exists.

CB-PR-002 was adapted independently by the gate-driver and sensing agents (and the thermal agent selected the NTC) with different NTC parts, bias networks and OTP thresholds, and the controller agent expects APWM from both drivers; the block needs a single owner.

summary: The gate-driver architecture (UCC21710-Q1 + UCC14141-Q1 per position, +15/-4 V, split R_G 10/3.3 ohm, DESAT 3.6 V with 288 ns blanking, cross-wired interlock, 150-250 ns dead time) is sound and 23 of 31 recomputed quantities agree with the agent to within rounding; the UCC21710-Q1 parameters and the UCC14141-Q1 isolation, UVLO/OVLO, PG and feedback data were confirmed from the TI datasheets fetched by the verifier. Corrections are required in four places: (1) the UCC14141-Q1 ratings were misread (1.5 W applies at TA <= 85 degC for 10.8-13.2 V, abs-max 2.5 W; the 1.2 W / 0.7 W rows are 25 V-output conditions) and the LS budget must be charged at 19 V (0.77-1.21 W depending on the LDO figure and the KR-IS-001 form); (2) the datasheet's COM-VEE regulator works through RLIM, so the shared LS supply must sink 28-46 mA of COM-return current, requiring RLIM <= 57-110 ohm (TI's 600 ohm absorbs 6 mA) and operating the RLIM pin outside its 16 %-run-time qualification - the dedicated sensing supply should become the baseline; (3) the parasitic-turn-on 'inherently immune' claim rests on a 1000 V small-signal ratio and understates the Miller charge by about 8x; a Q_GD-based estimate gives 3-6 V excursions, so the Miller clamp is required and the margin to the hot threshold is 0-3 V, not 5 V; (4) cross-area conflicts (LDO load 41 vs 23.1 mA, three different NTC implementations plus the unaddressed NTC insulation to the PE heatsink, TZ2 claimed twice, dead time 250 vs 200 ns) must be reconciled with the sensing, thermal, controller and assumptions agents. Minor items: unused AIN should be tied to COM per datasheet, the OC Schottky rationale is overstated (internal pull-down and 597 ns time constant), DESAT margins should include the R_DS(on) spread (trip 52-85 A, false-trip 1.35x worst case), the E_on penalty pair is internally inconsistent by 0.5 W, input capacitance falls to about 13 uF at 12 V bias, and KR-GD-012/KR-IS-001 applicability tags and conflicts need adjustment. Human-review rules were correctly surfaced and reference instance values were not copied except the acknowledged R_GS/Schottky parts.
